title: Toward constructing nanoscale hydroxo–lanthanide clusters: syntheses and characterizations of novel tetradecanuclear hydroxo–lanthanide clusters

material_class.structural_family: hollow Ln6 octahedron sharing two opposing apexes with two Ln5 square pyramids

synthesis.procedure: In a typical synthesis, 0.50 mmol of Ln(acac)3·4H2O (Ln = Tb) was dissolved in 5 mL of CH2Cl2 and 0.50 mmol of 2,2'-dipyridylsulfide in 2 mL of CH2Cl2 was added dropwise. The mixture was allowed to stand at room temperature overnight and the solution was concentrated. About 30 mL of hexane was added to the residue thereafter and the solution was refluxed for about 3 h. The resulting clear solution was kept at ambient temperature and cubic block crystals of 1 were obtained in 2–3 weeks. Elemental analysis was reported for vacuum-dried samples.
synthesis.temperature: room temperature overnight, then reflux ~3 h, then ambient temperature crystallization
synthesis.time: overnight standing; ~3 h reflux; crystals in 2–3 weeks
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution hydrolysis/concentration followed by hexane reflux and ambient crystallization
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: solution concentrated; ~30 mL hexane added; refluxed ~3 h; clear solution kept at ambient temperature to give cubic block crystals in 2–3 weeks

properties.summary: Complex 1 shows bright green Tb(III) luminescence in the solid state and CH2Cl2 solution via ligand-based (indirect) excitation; emission is typical of Tb(III). Solid-state emission is visibly brighter than Tb(acac)3·4H2O, attributed to increased rigidity. Relative quantum yield vs Tb(acac)3·4H2O in CH2Cl2 is ~0.53 at 298 K.

material_class.structural_family: isostructural to 1; hollow Ln6 octahedron sharing two opposing apexes with two Ln5 square pyramids

synthesis.procedure: Same typical synthesis as 1: 0.50 mmol of Ln(acac)3·4H2O (Ln = Eu) was dissolved in 5 mL of CH2Cl2 and 0.50 mmol of 2,2'-dipyridylsulfide in 2 mL of CH2Cl2 was added dropwise. The mixture was allowed to stand at room temperature overnight and concentrated. About 30 mL of hexane was added and the solution was refluxed for about 3 h. Cubic block crystals formed from the clear solution at ambient temperature in 2–3 weeks. Elemental analysis was reported for vacuum-dried samples (calc. for C120H186O66Eu14).

synthesis.time: overnight standing; ~3 h reflux; crystals in 2–3 weeks
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution hydrolysis/concentration followed by hexane reflux and ambient crystallization
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: solution concentrated; ~30 mL hexane added; refluxed ~3 h; crystals obtained at ambient temperature in 2–3 weeks

properties.summary: Compound 2 is only weakly red-luminescent in solution and the solid state with a typical Eu(III) emission spectrum. The solution excitation spectrum resembles that of 1, but the solid-state excitation spectrum is mostly characteristic of Eu(III), so ligand-assisted excitation appears ineffective and accounts for the low emission intensity.
